result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep every class name and every resolved value, and both pull the colors, radii and shadow into role-named variables. B goes further: it turns the button padding and border width into variables, works out the secondary button's padding from them so both buttons stay the same size, and explains why the one-off spacing and font sizes stay as literals. A is a bit tighter, but its hard-coded calc(10px - 1px) won't follow future padding changes, and it never says why spacing wasn't turned into variables. B's checklist does mention a disabled state the CSS doesn't have. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers keep every class name and the visible result, and both pull out the repeated colours, radii and shadow under role-based names. A is better on button size parity: it defines padding and border-width variables and works out the secondary button's padding from them, so the variants stay the same size if the padding changes. B hard-codes calc(10px - 1px), which keeps the size today but doesn't update with the main button's padding. Neither turns the spacing or font sizes into variables, though A says why. B's summary is slightly tighter, while A mentions a disabled state that the original CSS doesn't have and declares a border-width variable that the card rules never use.
